question.prompt: The solutions to the equations \(z^2 = 4 + 4\sqrt{15}\,i\) and \(z^2 = 2 + 2\sqrt{3}\,i,\) where \(i = \sqrt{-1},\) form the vertices of a parallelogram in the complex plane. The area of this parallelogram can be written in the form \(p\sqrt{q} - r\sqrt{s},\) where \(p,\) \(q,\) \(r,\) and \(s\) are positive integers and neither \(q\) nor \(s\) is divisible by the square of any prime number. What is \(p + q + r + s?\)

solutions.title: Complex roots and coordinate area
solutions.explanation:
Writing the complex roots in rectangular form will give the coordinates needed for an area calculation.

For the first equation, put \(z=a+bi\), where \(a,b\) are real. Expanding and comparing real and imaginary parts gives
\[
a^2-b^2=4,\qquad 2ab=4\sqrt{15}.
\]
The second equation implies \(a\ne0\) and \(b=\tfrac{2\sqrt{15}}a\). Substitution into the first yields
\[
a^2-\frac{60}{a^2}=4
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(a^2-10)(a^2+6)=0.
\]
Since \(a^2\ge0\), we have \(a^2=10\), and then \(b^2=6\). Also \(ab>0\), so the signs of \(a\) and \(b\) agree. The two roots are therefore
\[
\sqrt{10}+\sqrt6\,i\quad\text{and}\quad-\sqrt{10}-\sqrt6\,i.
\]
For the second equation, write \(z=c+di\). This time,
\[
c^2-d^2=2,\qquad cd=\sqrt3.
\]
Substituting \(d=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{c}\) gives
\[
c^4-2c^2-3=(c^2-3)(c^2+1)=0.
\]
Thus \(c^2=3\), \(d^2=1\), and their signs agree. These roots are \(\sqrt3+i\) and \(-\sqrt3-i\).

In the complex plane, name the four points
\[
P=(\sqrt{10},\sqrt6),\quad Q=(\sqrt3,1),\quad
R=(-\sqrt{10},-\sqrt6),\quad S=(-\sqrt3,-1).
\]
The opposite pairs \(P,R\) and \(Q,S\) share midpoint \((0,0)\), so they are the diagonals of the parallelogram. Hence \(P,Q,R,S\) is a boundary order.

The shoelace formula takes half the absolute difference of the two cyclic coordinate-product sums. Here those sums are
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_1&=\sqrt{10}-\sqrt{18}+\sqrt{10}-\sqrt{18}
=2\sqrt{10}-6\sqrt2,\\
S_2&=\sqrt{18}-\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{18}-\sqrt{10}
=6\sqrt2-2\sqrt{10}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the area is
\[
\frac12|S_1-S_2|
=\frac12\left|4\sqrt{10}-12\sqrt2\right|
=6\sqrt2-2\sqrt{10}.
\]
Both radicands are squarefree, so
\[
p+q+r+s=6+2+2+10=\boxed{20}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
